stem: ![](asset:P000169-stem-1) The velocity-displacement graph describing the motion of a bicycle is shown in the figure. The acceleration–displacement graph of the bicycle's motion is best described by:

assets.alt: Velocity v in m/s against position x in m: a straight line rising from 10 m/s at x = 0 to 50 m/s at x = 200 m, then constant at 50 m/s up to x = 400 m.
Acceleration a in m/s² against position x in m: rises along an upward-curving line from 2 at x = 0 to 10 at x = 200 m, then stays at 10 up to x = 400 m.
Acceleration a in m/s² against position x in m: rises in a straight line from 2 at x = 0 to 10 at x = 200 m, then drops to zero and stays at zero up to x = 400 m.
Acceleration a in m/s² against position x in m: rises in a straight line from 2 at x = 0 to 10 at x = 200 m, then stays at 10 up to x = 400 m.
Acceleration a in m/s² against position x in m: rises along an upward-curving line from 2 at x = 0 to 10 at x = 200 m, then drops to zero and stays at zero up to x = 400 m.

Two graphs side by side. Left: velocity in m/s against x in m, rising from 10 to 50 at 200 m, then flat to 400 m. Right: acceleration in m/s² against x, rising in a straight line from 2 to 10 at 200 m, then zero to 400 m.
